resources.string: Blocks Reels, Shorts and non-followed feed posts

ShortBlock reads the screen content of Instagram and YouTube only, in order to detect Reels, Shorts and algorithmic feed posts and navigate away from them. Nothing is stored or sent anywhere — the app has no internet permission.
ShortBlock works through an accessibility service. Three steps, in this order — step 2 stays greyed out until step 1 is done.

Android 13 and newer block accessibility for sideloaded apps. In the app info screen tap the ⋮ menu at the top right and choose “Allow restricted settings”. If that entry is missing, this step is already done.
Under “Installed apps” / “Downloaded apps” pick ShortBlock and switch it on.
Recommended on Xiaomi, Samsung and OnePlus devices — they stop background services aggressively.
Service is off — nothing is being blocked
Closes the Reels viewer, no matter whether it was opened from the tab, from Explore or from a DM. Stories stay untouched.
Forces the chronological “Following” feed and stops at the end of it, before the suggested posts start.
Closes the Shorts player and the Shorts tab. Normal videos, search and subscriptions keep working.
No internet permission, no analytics, nothing leaves the device.
If the app closed something it should not have: this is the rule that fired. Report the line and it can be narrowed down.
When Instagram or YouTube change their layout, blocking silently stops working. Turn this on, open the screen that is no longer blocked, come back here and copy the matching IDs into Rules.kt.
Nothing recorded yet. Turn recording on and open Instagram or YouTube.
Please switch to “Following” at the top left
